clue.text: An environment that's very limiting for flight or walk

definitions.text: An environment that's very limiting for flight or walk

parts.words: An environment that's very limiting for flight or walk
parts.note: a home for a pet bird gives it little room to fly, and the same word names a London street ending in Walk, beside St James's Park

explanation.definitionFit: A small wire enclosure for a pet songbird hardly allows flying, and London's well-known street by St James's Park bears the same name before Walk.

clue.text: Baseball's number one American guy?

indicators.note: the number one of a word is its opening letter, here of the word Baseball's

parts.note: Abe is a typical American man's name, as in Abe Lincoln

explanation.surface: A question about who was the top American player in baseball.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: Babe Ruth was baseball's greatest American star.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe Ruth, nicknamed by his first name alone, is often called baseball's greatest ever player.

clue.text: Reason android has no heart

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for android is dropped, as a heartless body would lack its middle

parts.note: an android is a humanlike robot

explanation.surface: A machine-man without feelings, which explains its behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no heart' removes B, the middle letter of ROBOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of a problem is its underlying cause or reason, a common synonym.

clue.text: The drink, not half powerful, has vessel capsizing

indicators.note: only half of the word for powerful is kept, its second three letters going

parts.note: a cogent argument is powerful and convincing

indicators.note: a capsized vessel is upside down, so in a down clue the word is turned over

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: A strong spirit served while a ship overturns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' leaves COG from COGENT; 'capsizing' turns CAN into NAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a familiar after-dinner drink.

clue.text: What dancing angels would do? Stop waffling!

definitions.meaning: the old scholastic question of how many angels can dance on the head of a pin means they must reach its tip
an order to come straight to the essential matter without padding

explanation.definitionFit: To come to the point means speaking directly about what matters; literally the angels would arrive at the pin's tip.

clue.text: Nurse makes visit around five with drug

indicators.note: the visiting word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit them
V is the Roman numeral five
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A nurse pays a house call with a dose of medicine at five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts VE inside CALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Cavell was the British nurse executed in the First World War for helping Allied soldiers escape.

clue.text: Republic's chaps taken in by heretic

definitions.note: possessive adjective, matching an adjective meaning belonging to that former Soviet republic

indicators.note: the word for chaps is held inside the word for heretic

parts.note: an Arian followed Arius, whose doctrine was condemned as heresy
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A nation's men are deceived by a religious dissenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' looks like 'fooled by', but here it signals a container. Arius was a 4th-century priest whose teaching was condemned as heresy.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenian means of or belonging to Armenia, a republic in the Caucasus.

clue.text: Have food briefly before walking in old part of county

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to have food is to eat
striding is walking with long steps

explanation.surface: Grabbing a quick bite before a walk somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims EAT to EA. The East Riding was one of the three old divisions of Yorkshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Riding was a historic division of Yorkshire, revived later as a unitary area.

clue.text: Spots socialite reeling after end of ball

indicators.note: the jumbled word comes after the single letter
the last letter of the word ball is taken
reeling means staggering about, so the letters of socialite are jumbled

explanation.surface: A party girl staggering home after the dance ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse lists the anagram first, but 'after' puts L, the end of 'ball', in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots and localities are both places or particular sites, as nouns.

clue.text: Unpleasant time in bar — after spinning round, was sick

indicators.note: the unpleasant time goes inside the turned bar
the word for bar is turned back to front

parts.note: a pub is a bar
rough means unpleasant, as in a rough time

explanation.surface: After a rough night at the pub and a spinning head, someone threw up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning round' turns PUB into BUP, and 'in' puts ROUGHT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up food is to vomit, so the past phrase means was sick.

clue.text: Actress about to lay in bad craft shop

indicators.note: the hen's word goes inside the jumbled shop letters
bad suggests something wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: eggy is a dictionary word for a hen ready to produce eggs

explanation.surface: An actress is about to put something down in a messy little craft store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion. 'Eggy' is an uncommon dictionary sense: a hen about to lay. 'lay' tempts you to think of setting something down.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Peggy Ashcroft was a celebrated English actress of stage and screen.

clue.text: It has the like of Polyhymnia mostly in charge?

definitions.text: It has the like of Polyhymnia mostly in charge?

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: Polyhymnia is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A question about whether a goddess of song runs this art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts MUSE to MUS. Read whole, the clue defines the art the Muses preside over.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyhymnia was the Muse of sacred song, so this art is overseen by such a goddess.

clue.text: Previous PM — popular and modern person pressing claims of polymathy?

definitions.text: modern person pressing claims of polymathy?

parts.note: John Major was a British prime minister in the 1990s
general means widespread or popular, as in general appeal

explanation.surface: A former prime minister, well liked and up to date, boasting of wide learning.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan's Pirates of Penzance has the song 'I am the very model of a modern Major-General', listing all the knowledge he claims.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic officer in the operetta boasts of expertise in every subject while being a modern military man.

clue.text: Cherry makes stain when getting on material

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or stain
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
chino is a cotton twill fabric

explanation.surface: A cherry leaves a mark when dropped on cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes stain' reads as a cherry marking fabric, but 'stain' is just MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A maraschino is a cherry preserved in a liqueur, used in cocktails.

clue.text: Composer has country house, very large, in which ball is held

indicators.note: the ball is placed inside the joined house and size words
together with in which, this says one piece is held within the others

parts.note: a villa is a country house
OS is the abbreviation for outsize
a lob is a high ball in tennis or cricket

explanation.surface: A composer owns a huge country mansion where a dance takes place.
explanation.walkthrough: The container signal is split, 'in which' ... 'is held', with the ball between. 'ball' suggests a dance held at the house. Heitor Villa-Lobos was a Brazilian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Heitor Villa-Lobos was the best-known Brazilian composer of classical music.

clue.text: A team's seen as an old enemy

parts.note: XI is eleven, a cricket or football team, and the 's is kept as S

explanation.surface: A sports side is regarded as an old rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of team's gives the S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis powers, Germany, Italy and Japan, were the Allies' enemies in the Second World War.

clue.text: Mark time at the beginning?

parts.note: read as a dot marking when time started, rather than marching on the spot

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a very long time ago, as if dating from the very start of time.

clue.text: Unfashionable scooter-rider exposed as gay touring round

indicators.note: the exposed word goes round the rider

parts.note: to be outed is to have one's homosexuality revealed
a Mod was a 1960s British youth who rode a motor scooter

explanation.surface: A scooter rider revealed as gay while out touring is behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring round' signals a container. Mods were a 1960s British youth culture known for Vespa and Lambretta scooters.
explanation.definitionFit: Outmoded means old-fashioned, no longer in style.

clue.text: Popular Les, flexible and useful in many ways

indicators.note: flexible means bendable, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A man called Les is well liked, adaptable and handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' rearranges POPULAR LES.
explanation.definitionFit: All-purpose describes something serving every use, versatile.

clue.text: Girl's demeanour puts Mister Outsider off

definitions.note: read as 'Girl is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: the abbreviation for mister is removed from the outside of the demeanour word

parts.note: manner is demeanour or bearing

explanation.surface: A girl's manners put off a stranger called Mister Outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outsider off' strips M and R, the first and last letters of MANNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne is a common girl's name.

clue.text: Toxic litre — alcohol, knocking number out

indicators.note: with out, this says a piece is struck from the alcohol word
completes knocking out, removal of the number abbreviation

parts.note: ethanol is the chemical name for drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A litre of hooch without its number is poisonous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking ... out' removes NO from ETHANOL, leaving ETHAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal means deadly, and toxic substances can be deadly.

clue.text: Nelson was given about 2,000 in newspaper coverage

definitions.meaning: Nelson's Column in Trafalgar Square is about 169 feet tall, close to 2,000 inches
the amount of space a story gets in a newspaper, measured by length of printed column

explanation.definitionFit: Journalists measure space by column length, and Nelson's monument stands roughly that many inches high.

clue.text: Saw illiterate children

definitions.meaning: a nonstandard past tense of see
... means offspring, as in the ... of Abraham

explanation.definitionFit: Seed is dialect past tense of see, and also biblical for descendants or offspring.

clue.text: A pitch showing evidence of fire?

parts.note: to shy is to throw or pitch, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A throw that suggests there's been a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like tar or a sports field, but it is a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means covered with ash, residue left after burning.

clue.text: Fix one gong on to front of DJ

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
gong is slang for a medal or honour, and an MBE is a British honour

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word DJ is taken

explanation.surface: One medal is fixed onto the front of a dinner jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is British slang for an honour such as the MBE; DJ here suggests a dinner jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbed, a variant of embed, is to fix firmly in place.

clue.text: Ineffective as gum without attachments

definitions.meaning: gums without teeth attached to them

explanation.definitionFit: Toothless figuratively means lacking force, and literally describes gums bare of teeth.

clue.text: The leg properly positioned to receive ball?

definitions.meaning: in cricket the leg side is also called the ...
in football a player not offside may legally receive a pass

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the on side is the leg side; in football or rugby a player is allowed to play the ball when not offside.

clue.text: Make dolly sit in a rather lumpish way?

indicators.note: to make something of letters is to form them into a new word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting a toy doll to sit up is clumsy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' tells you to form a new word from DOLLY SIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolidly means impassively and heavily, much like being lumpish.
